_meta.companion: data/presets_sources.json (round 1: HIRES, MIKE, HARPS, LRIS, DESI); same structure. Keys SCOL and MAL65 point to the round-1 files.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short quote from the saved document. derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values. alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). Every quote was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text (whitespace/glyph-normalised).
_meta.quote_normalisation: Quotes copied from pdftotext / HTML text; degree glyphs (◦ ˚ º) and double primes normalised; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces; table rows quoted as whitespace-separated cells.

deimos.title: Keck II / DEIMOS (multi-object slit spectrograph, tiltable plane reflection gratings)
deimos.recommended_preset: 1200G grating (1200 l/mm, gold), central wavelength 8000 A (grating tilt alpha = 53.459 deg in the Faber design table), 0.75" slit, 8192-px (2 x 4096, 15 um) dispersion axis. Validate against the Faber design table row (0.324 A/px = 21.602 A/mm, 6673-9294 A without gaps, effective FWHM 1.35 A -> R ~ 5900 DERIVED) and the Keck grating table (0.33 A/px, 2630 A, FWHM 1.1-1.6 A for 0.75"). Fully self-consistent alternative: 600ZD at 7000 A (alpha = 35.337 deg; 0.648 A/px; 4414-9654 A; FWHM 3.55 A). The 1200G blaze ANGLE on the Keck page (26.7 deg) is inconsistent with its blaze wavelength (see Conflicts); the angle only affects the efficiency curve, not dispersion/coverage.

All DEIMOS numbers here come from Keck/UCO web documents and the 2002 Keck telescope guide.
CCD gap widths in pixels (only the 0.4' x 5.0' imaging-field loss).

Measured (as opposed to tabulated) resolution per grating; the Keck FWHM values are not flagged as predictions but no measurement method is given.
Blaze angle of 1200G consistent with its blaze wavelength (see Conflicts).
conflicts: Spectrograph (camera-collimator) angle: 44.451 deg vs 44.51 deg, both on KDGINFO; the table rows reproduce 44.451.

Pixel scale: 0.1185"/px (KDSPEC) vs 0.119"/px (KTG02, KDPRED) vs 0.00759"/um (KDSPEC and KTG02; = 0.1139"/px, inconsistent with the 0.1185 on the same row) vs 0.1193"/px DERIVED from f/15 (149.6 m) and 86.50/15.00.

1200G blaze: 7760 A / 776 nm (KDGRAT) vs 7500 A (KDSPEC "1200 l/mm (7500 Å blaze; gold-coated)"; KTG02). Blaze angle 26.7 deg (KDGRAT) gives a Littrow blaze of 2 sin(26.7)/1200 = 7489 A (DERIVED), matching 7500 A, not 7760 A; 26.7 deg is also the angle listed for the out-of-service 1200L (750 nm).
830G: blaze 8640 A vs blaze angle 20.566 deg -> Littrow 8457 A (DERIVED, 2% lower). 600ZD (13.00 deg -> 7498 A), 900ZD (14.33 deg -> 5500 A) and 1200B (15.7 deg -> 4510 A) are self-consistent.
Camera: "eight-element" lens (KDOVER, as built) vs "nine lenses and one window" (DCDR95, 1995 design).
Spectral length basis: "(8000 px)" (KDSPEC, KTG02) vs "(8192 px)" (KDGRAT); same Angstrom values.
Nominal design slit: 1.0" (KDSPEC) vs 0.75" (KDPRED 1999); the FWHM values in all tables are for 0.75".
notes: DEIMOS was designed for two cameras fed by a common collimator; only one camera was built (KDSPEC: "Capacity for two cameras fed from common collimator; only one camera presently built").

Geometry check (DERIVED): with camera-collimator angle 44.451 deg and f_cam = 381.0 mm, the grating equation sin(alpha) + sin(beta) = m g lambda reproduces every tested Faber-table row (lambda_0 to 0.2 A, A/mm to 0.001).

Blaze in the DEIMOS geometry (DERIVED, for the app's efficiency curve): the facet-normal condition alpha + beta = 2 theta_B with alpha - beta = 44.451 gives lambda_blaze = 2 sin(theta_B) cos(22.226 deg)/g = 0.9257 x Littrow value: 600ZD ~6940 A, 1200G ~6930 A (if 26.7 deg is right), 830G ~7830 A.

The Faber table is a 1995 design calculation (corrected Nov 1997); the Keck summary table gives the operational values. Both agree on dispersion (0.648 vs 0.65 A/px for 600 l/mm; 0.324-0.328 vs 0.33 A/px for 1200 l/mm).

xshooter.title: VLT / X-Shooter (three prism-cross-dispersed echelle arms: UVB, VIS, NIR)
xshooter.recommended_preset: All three arms with the standard slits UVB 1.0", VIS 0.9", NIR 0.9" (11" long). Echelles: UVB 180 gr/mm, 41.77 deg; VIS 99.4 gr/mm, 54.0 deg; NIR 55 gr/mm, 46.07 deg; in-plane offset 0.0 deg, off-plane gamma 2.2 / 2.0 / 1.8 deg. Cross-dispersers (all double pass): UVB one 60 deg silica prism; VIS one 49 deg SCHOTT SF6 prism; NIR one 35 deg Infrasil + two 22 deg ZnSe prisms (cryogenic, ~105 K). XUM24 has no NIR 1.5" row (slit removed 2011).
Overall R range: 4,000-17,000 (V11 abstract) vs 3000-18000 (XUM24 Sec. 1.2) vs 4 000-14 000 (M120, D06 design era).

Dichroic crossovers: 559.5 / 1024 nm (V11) vs 557 / 1019 nm (M120, design) vs 550 / 1000 nm (K08).
NIR temperature: optics at 105 K (V11, K08, N08) vs "operates at 79 K" (XUM24 Sec. 2.2.4); detector 81 K (V11, K08) vs 79 K (XUM24 Table 9).
Spatial pixel scale: 0.164 / 0.154 / 0.245"/px (XUM24, projected slit) vs ~0.15 / ~0.15 / ~0.20 (V11 Fig. 9) vs 0.140 / 0.135 / 0.218 DERIVED from the detector plate scales.

Blaze wavelengths vs echelle constants (DERIVED): 2 sin(theta_B) cos(gamma)/g = 7396 nm (UVB), 16268 nm (VIS), 26176 nm (NIR). Tabulated m x lambda_blaze (V11 Table 3): UVB 7493 (order 24) falling to 7434 (order 14) and 7228 (order 13, in the dichroic crossover); VIS 16515 (order 30) falling to 16274 (order 17) and 16026 (order 16); NIR 26150 +/- 1.5 nm for all 16 orders. NIR agrees with the sourced echelle constants to 0.1%; the UVB/VIS 'blaze wavelength' column drifts with order (VIS by 3%), so it is not a clean validation target for the blaze function.
notes: Consistency check (DERIVED): the Littrow dispersion computed from the sourced echelle constants and the DERIVED effective camera focal lengths (270/280/177 mm) reproduces the dispersion implied by XUM24 Table 13 to 4% (UVB), 1.4% (VIS) and 1.1% (NIR) -- supporting the beam (100/100/85 mm) + camera f/# derivation.

Echelle geometry (interpretation): 'off-blaze angle' = in-plane offset theta = 0.0 deg in all arms (B08 Sec. 2 uses the same term: 'an Echelle grating with constant σE at off-blaze angle θ'); 'off-plane angle' = gamma (2.2 / 2.0 / 1.8 deg); N08 calls the NIR echelle 'near-Littrow'.
UVB and VIS share an ESO FIERA controller; UVB/VIS have ADCs, NIR does not (V11 Sec. 2.2.7).
M120 (2005) is a PDR-era design: NIR 1.03-2.48 um 'in 15 orders', four-lens camera; D06 (2006 FDR) introduced the slower F/2.1 NIR camera.

Sellmeier_SCHOTT.form: n^2(lambda) - 1 = B1 lambda^2/(lambda^2 - C1) + B2 lambda^2/(lambda^2 - C2) + B3 lambda^2/(lambda^2 - C3)
Sellmeier_SCHOTT.wavelength_unit: um (C in um^2); valid 'from the near UV to 2.3 um'
Sellmeier_SCHOTT.quote: the refractive indices for any wavelength within the range from the near UV to 2.3 µm can be calculated with the help of the constants B1, B2, B3, and C1,C2,C3. When calculating the refractive index using the Sellmeier coefficients from the SCHOTT data sheets, the wavelength λ needs to be entered in units of µm.

Sellmeier_Heraeus.form: n^2 - 1 = B1 lambda^2/(lambda^2 - C1) + B2 lambda^2/(lambda^2 - C2) + B3 lambda^2/(lambda^2 - C3)
Sellmeier_Heraeus.quote: n2 - 1 = B1 λ 2 /(λ 2 - C1) + B2 λ 2 /(λ 2 - C2 ) + B3 λ 2 /(λ 2 -C3 ) ... Wavelength λ in μm at 20°C

Sellmeier_CHARMS_T.form: n^2(lambda,T) - 1 = sum_{i=1..3} S_i(T) lambda^2/(lambda^2 - lambda_i(T)^2), with S_i(T) = sum_{j=0..4} S_ij T^j and lambda_i(T) = sum_{j=0..4} lambda_ij T^j
Sellmeier_CHARMS_T.wavelength_unit: lambda and lambda_i in um, T in K; ABSOLUTE index (in vacuum)
Sellmeier_CHARMS_T.loc: Sec. 3 (worked BaF2 example at 1.0 um, 77 K)
Sellmeier_CHARMS_T.quote: Si (T) = ∑ Sij ⋅ T j ... λ i (T) = ∑ λ ij ⋅ T j
